My parents love showing me videos of them harvesting rice with other adults in our tribe. Honestly, I cannot think of a more boring way to spend a Saturday, but I know I have to go.

"Waabooz," says my grandfather. He hands me the two long wooden sticks used for harvesting rice. I hesitate before reaching out to take them. "Speaking of which," Reba said, pulling Harper's bracelet out of her pocket, "I meant to give this to you earlier."
"Thanks!" Harper said. "Is it okay if I don't want to lend it again?"
